claims.claim: RHO c.68C>A (p.Pro23His) is classified as pathogenic for retinitis pigmentosa.
Human rhodopsin is UniProt P08100 and is encoded by RHO.
P23H opsin shows structural instability, ER retention, and ER-associated degradation in the cited experimental literature.
YC-001 improved P23H opsin trafficking in cell assays and was characterized as a non-retinoid pharmacological chaperone.
YC-001 also showed inverse-agonist and noncompetitive antagonist behavior toward rod opsin signaling, creating a functional tradeoff that must be measured.
Later P23H mouse and retinal-explant work remained preclinical and reported micromolar YC-001 effects on rhodopsin localization.
YC-001 improved cell-surface trafficking of human RHO P23H in a heterologous NIH3T3 expression system, with a weaker effect than reported for mouse P23H.
Intravitreal YC-001 microparticles temporarily improved scotopic ERG, retinal-layer thickness, and photoreceptor counts in Rho P23H/+ mice; effects disappeared after clearance.
YC-001 produced a bovine-opsin Trp-fluorescence EC50 of 0.98 +/- 0.05 uM, but direct stabilization of purified P23H mutant opsin has not been demonstrated.

current_inference: YC-001 now has a connected preclinical chain from opsin binding through human-P23H cellular trafficking to temporary P23H-mouse retinal protection. Direct human-mutant binding, durable exposure, human photoreceptor survival, and patient benefit remain unresolved. YC-054 and YC-068 have not inherited YC-001's external validation.
